mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen each of the last three weeks (-35.7 to -28.6), indicating a steady return of commuting activity. This sustained recovery should continue feeding weekday retail footfall, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the last four.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -35.7 to -28.6 over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is not higher than prior 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility crosses above -20 (i.e., weekly value exceeds -20 for the first time in the series), it signals a critical mass of commuters/shoppers returning to public transport, which should drive a rapid uptick in RETAIL_REC within the following two weeks as transit-dependent retail catchments reactivate.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly value rises above -20 percent from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -32.3 to -23.9 over the snapshot period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks after TRANSIT crosses the -20 threshold, or TRANSIT never crosses the threshold and RETAIL_REC still rises.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent improvement in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates a joint commuting-and-transit recovery that compounds to produce a larger retail rebound than either series would predict alone, because workers both leave home and use shared transport to reach retail districts.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved monotonically across the four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over next 4 weeks is no greater than the growth predicted by either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone (no interaction effect observed), or RETAIL_REC declines despite joint improvement.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS swing from +12.3 to -2.1 and back to +4.6 reflects weather-driven outdoor activity volatility rather than policy change. In a regime of unstable weather, PARKS fluctuations do not transmit to RETAIL_REC because park visits and retail trips are substitute rather than complementary activities, so RETAIL_REC should remain flat to slightly negative over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS week-on-week swing exceeds 10 points in absolute value
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung from 12.3 to -2.1 to 4.6 across three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises more than 2 points in the week following a large PARKS swing, indicating the series are positively linked rather than substitutive.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has been declining steadily (7.6 to 4.7) over the snapshot, indicating people are spending less time confined at home. This behavioral loosening is a leading indicator of discretionary trips, which should raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 7.6 to 4.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days even as RESIDENTIAL continues to decline, or RESIDENTIAL reverses upward while RETAIL_REC still rises.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility rising from -9.4 to -5.1 suggests relaxation of restrictions on essential-adjacent retail, often a leading policy signal that precedes loosening of restrictions on non-essential retail. If this trend continues, RETAIL_REC should follow with a lagged rise within two weeks as policy restrictions on broader retail categories ease in tandem.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved monotonically from -9.4 to -5.1 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM's third consecutive weekly increase, breaking the presumed policy-lag linkage.

mechanism_narrative: Under a regime where restrictions are actively tightening (evidenced by simultaneous negative WORKPLACES and TRANSIT levels well below baseline alongside elevated RESIDENTIAL), any residual improvement in RETAIL_REC is likely a temporary pre-tightening rebound that will reverse once enforcement catches up, driving RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain below -25 while RESIDENTIAL remains above +3
evidence_refs: fact:all three series remain in restrictive territory (WORKPLACES -28.6, TRANSIT -23.9, RESIDENTIAL +4.7) at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next 4 weeks despite WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and RESIDENTIAL remaining in the restrictive band, contradicting the tightening-regime reversal thesis.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC itself has been roughly flat for the last two weeks (-25.7, -25.4) after a brief improvement, suggesting behavioral habituation to a new steady-state retail pattern. In a steady-state regime, the recent flat trend is the best predictor of near-term behavior, implying RETAIL_REC will remain essentially unchanged (near-zero net direction) over the next week rather than continuing the earlier recovery trajectory.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC values were -25.7 and -25.4 over the last two weeks, essentially flat
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows a clear upward move (greater than 2 points) over the next week, contradicting the flat-habituation prediction.
